messages:
ryan: Heads-up: onboarding CustNimbus LoRA (nimbus-base-v1 + cust-nimbus-lora) to staging. After int4 quant + stitch we see cents dropped in invoice outputs (e.g. '£1,234.50' -> '£1,234'). Need a quick triage and a small eval pack.
maya: Oof. Share pack path + CLI + tokenizer in the model manifest?
ryan: s3://redwood-evals/custnimbus/nimbus_onboard/4367001122/ (invoices_10.json). CLI: `rdw-infer --model nimbus-base-v1+cust-nimbus-lora --quant int4 --input invoices_10.json --out out.json --batch 2`. Manifest tokenizer: hf/byte-level-1. My dev env used hf/byte-level-3 accidentally.
zhou: Can you paste a failing example and token splits?
ryan: Example: prompt: "Invoice: £2,345.60" expected same, got "Invoice: £2,345". Tokenize results: byte-level-1 -> ['2', ',', '345', '.', '60'] ; byte-level-3 -> ['2', ',', '345', '.', '6', '0']
tess: Looks like byte-level-3 splits cents into two one-digit tokens which are fragile on our int4 decode path. Seen before. Two mitigations: (1) enforce tokenizer_compat in manifest; (2) small runtime decode guard to keep single-digit tokens after '.' sticky; (3) last-resort postproc regex to reformat obvious amounts.
eval-bot: Quick eval (initial): fp16 cents-preserved: 10/10, int8: 9/10, int4: 6/10. Failures cluster on splits like ['.', '6', '0'].
zhou: I'll run token inspector and a micro-benchmark across fp16/int8/int4 on the 10-case pack and output exact-match + numeric MSE.
maya: Meanwhile add a manifest override `tokenizer_compat: hf/byte-level-1` for CustNimbus and a unit test in the manifest repo to catch this class of regressions. Also open a low-risk draft PR for the runtime guard if we need to patch quickly.
ryan: Thanks. Demo scheduled in 4 days. If we can canary the runtime change to staging and flip tokenizer_compat, that should buy time. Ping here with links to PRs and bench CSV. :thumbsup:
